summary: Jinshi Fan is a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University under Bai Su (~1958–1963). She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and as a part-time professor and doctoral supervisor at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng was a scholar in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He was deputy director in the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and later served as a researcher (professor) at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).

Jiro Abe was a Japanese philosopher and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita was a scholar in Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943). He held academic appointments at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1963–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1992).
Jiro Murata was a scholar of archaeology and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and later held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1968).

Jiro Sugiyama was a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1954). He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1988), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1988–1993), ICPBS (~1996–2004), and Bukkyo University.
Jiryo Masuda, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under Unrai Wogihara. He served as a professor at the University of Calcutta and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea was an Indologist and historian who studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918). He served as the Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1959) and taught Sarasi Kumar Saraswati.

Jitendra Nath Mohanty was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, Emory, and Temple University (~1986), and founded Husserl Studies.
Jitsuaki Oshika is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University and served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara was an East and Central Asian historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He held posts at the Third Higher School, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan is a researcher in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Laxmidhar Behera (attested 2023) and holds a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren was a scholar of religion, philosophy, and Buddhism. He studied at Peking University under Lin He and Yongtong Tang, taught at Peking University (1942–1964), directed the CASS Institute of World Religions (1964–1986), and directed the National Library.
Jo Khyab Pema Trinlé Nyingpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo.

Joachim Gentz is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and later served as Reader and Professor (attested 2013, 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer at the University of Vienna, earning his Magister degree by 1994.

Joachim Wach was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Leipzig, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Freiberg, and Leiden. He taught at Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

Joan Halifax is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Newcomb College and Union Institute & University under teachers including Seungsahn Haengwon and Bernie Glassman. She worked at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard, and founded Upaya Zen Center.
Joanna Cook is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed her studies under the supervision of James Laidlaw. She holds an academic post at Christ's College, University of Cambridge.
